slides.texte_overlay:
why you feel tired all the time
(and what actually helps)

you're not drinking water

mild dehydration feels exactly like fatigue. drink a full glass of water as soon as you wake up and another before every meal, and notice the difference by day three.

your mornings are dark

staying indoors under dim light keeps your body half asleep. step outside for ten minutes before noon, even when it's cloudy, and your energy wakes up with you.

your mind is understimulated

a brain fed only on scrolling feels foggy and flat. 5 minutes a day learning something real, like a planet or a painting, wakes it up like nothing else.
slides.texte_sophia:
your mind is understimulated

my brain felt foggy and flat from scrolling all day. i do it with the Sophia app now, one lesson a day: a planet, a painting. 5 minutes of something real woke my mind up.

slides.texte_overlay:
your screen time runs late

bright screens at midnight push your sleep later and make it lighter. stopping an hour before bed is the easiest energy boost there is, and it costs nothing.

you sit all day

sitting for hours slows everything down, including your mood. stand up and walk for five minutes every hour, and the afternoon slump becomes much smaller.
